path-canvas.geometry.centre.note: Name of a snap guide in the drawing canvas: the middle line of the frame. Read out to screen reader users.

path-canvas.geometry.corner.note: Lower case word for a type of point: a sharp bend with no curve. Used inside sentences such as Point 2 of 5, corner. Not a corner of the screen.

path-canvas.geometry.edge.note: Name of a snap guide in the drawing canvas: the edge of the frame or of another shape. Read out to screen reader users.

path-canvas.geometry.n.note: Count of points on a path. {n} is the number of points. Inserted into longer sentences such as Path, 4 points, closed.

vars.n: The count the text is about.

path-canvas.geometry.n-degrees.note: An angle. {n} is the angle in degrees, rounded as it is shown.

vars.n: The count the text is about.

path-canvas.geometry.safe-area-edge.note: Name of a snap guide in the drawing canvas: the border of the area where content is not clipped. Read out to screen reader users.

path-canvas.geometry.smooth.note: Lower case word for a type of point: a curved point whose two handles may differ in length. Used inside sentences such as Point 2 of 5, smooth.

path-canvas.geometry.symmetric.note: Lower case word for a type of point: a curved point whose two handles are always equal in length. Used inside sentences such as Point 2 of 5, symmetric.

path-canvas.mc-path-canvas.all-points-se.note: Screen reader announcement. {points} is a count with its noun, such as 4 points.

vars.points: The value that replaces points in the text.

path-canvas.mc-path-canvas.arrow-keys-mo.text: Arrow keys move the cursor or the selected point. Enter places a point, or closes the path on its first point. Tab steps through points. C switches smooth and corner. Delete removes a point.
path-canvas.mc-path-canvas.arrow-keys-mo.note: Keyboard instructions for the drawing canvas in pen mode, read by screen readers. Keep the key names Enter, Tab, C and Delete as on a keyboard. Smooth and corner are the two point types.

path-canvas.mc-path-canvas.arrow-keys-mo.text: Arrow keys move the in handle.
path-canvas.mc-path-canvas.arrow-keys-mo.note: Screen reader hint when the incoming curve handle of a point is selected. The in handle controls the curve arriving at the point; do not confuse with the out handle.

path-canvas.mc-path-canvas.arrow-keys-mo.text: Arrow keys move the out handle.
path-canvas.mc-path-canvas.arrow-keys-mo.note: Screen reader hint when the outgoing curve handle of a point is selected. The out handle controls the curve leaving the point; do not confuse with the in handle.
Screen reader hint when a point on a path is selected.

path-canvas.mc-path-canvas.cursor-at-x-x.text: Cursor at x {x}, y {y}. Press Enter to place a point.
path-canvas.mc-path-canvas.cursor-at-x-x.note: Screen reader announcement in pen mode. {x} and {y} are the cursor's horizontal and vertical position on the canvas, as numbers. Keep the key name Enter.

vars.x: The value that replaces x in the text.
vars.y: The value that replaces y in the text.

path-canvas.mc-path-canvas.drawing-canva.note: Lower case accessible name of the area where paths are drawn. Appended to a description of the canvas for screen readers.

path-canvas.mc-path-canvas.handle-delete.note: Screen reader announcement after a curve handle of a point was removed.

path-canvas.mc-path-canvas.n-points-sele.note: Screen reader announcement. {n} is the number of selected points, always more than one.

vars.n: The value that replaces n in the text.

path-canvas.mc-path-canvas.path-closed.note: Screen reader announcement after the last point was joined to the first, making a closed shape.

path-canvas.mc-path-canvas.path-deleted.note: Screen reader announcement after a whole path was removed. A path is one drawn line or shape.

path-canvas.mc-path-canvas.path-points-c.note: Accessible name of a closed path (its ends are joined). {points} is a count with its noun, such as 4 points. Compare Path, {points}, open.

vars.points: The value that replaces points in the text.

path-canvas.mc-path-canvas.path-points-o.note: Accessible name of an open path (its ends are not joined). {points} is a count with its noun, such as 4 points. Compare Path, {points}, closed.

vars.points: The value that replaces points in the text.

path-canvas.mc-path-canvas.point-added-p.note: Screen reader announcement after one point was added. {points} is the new total as a count with its noun, such as 5 points.

vars.points: The value that replaces points in the text.

path-canvas.mc-path-canvas.point-deleted.note: Screen reader announcement after points were removed. {deleted} is how many points were removed; {points} is the new total as a count with its noun, such as 3 points.

vars.deleted: The count the text is about.
vars.points: The value that replaces points in the text.

path-canvas.mc-path-canvas.point-n-is-no.note: Screen reader announcement after a point changed type. {n} is the point's position in the path, starting at 1. {kind} is one of the words smooth, symmetric or corner.

vars.kind: The value that replaces kind in the text.
vars.n: The value that replaces n in the text.

path-canvas.mc-path-canvas.point-n-of-to.note: Accessible name of a point. {n} is its position, starting at 1. {total} is the number of points on the path. {kind} is smooth, symmetric or corner. {x} and {y} are its coordinates.

vars.kind: The value that replaces kind in the text.
vars.n: The value that replaces n in the text.
vars.total: The value that replaces total in the text.
vars.x: The value that replaces x in the text.
vars.y: The value that replaces y in the text.

path-canvas.mc-path-canvas.points.note: Label of the list or toolbar group of points of the selected path. A plural noun.

path-canvas.mc-path-canvas.rotation.note: Label of the angle readout while a selection is turned. Shown with a value in degrees.

path-canvas.mc-path-canvas.selection-cle.note: Screen reader announcement after the user deselected all points and paths.

path-canvas.mc-path-canvas.tab-steps-thr.text: Tab steps through points. Arrow keys move the selected point. C switches smooth and corner. Delete removes a point. Escape deselects.
path-canvas.mc-path-canvas.tab-steps-thr.note: Keyboard instructions for the drawing canvas in select mode, read by screen readers. Keep the key names Tab, C, Delete and Escape as on a keyboard.

path-canvas.mc-path-canvas.this-path-has.text: This path has {max} points, the most you can add. Move, delete or change them instead.
path-canvas.mc-path-canvas.this-path-has.note: Message when the point limit is reached. {max} is the largest number of points one path may have.

vars.max: The value that replaces max in the text.

path-canvas.mc-path-canvas.this-point-ha.text: This point has no handles. Press C to make it smooth.
path-canvas.mc-path-canvas.this-point-ha.note: Screen reader hint for a corner point without curve handles. Keep the key name C. Smooth is the point type that has handles.

path-canvas.mc-path-canvas.w-w-h-h.note: Size readout while scaling a selection. W is width and H is height, abbreviated. {w} and {h} are numbers.

vars.h: The value that replaces h in the text.
vars.w: The value that replaces w in the text.

path-canvas.mc-path-canvas.which.text: {which, select, in {In handle of point {n}, x {x}, y {y}.} other {Out handle of point {n}, x {x}, y {y}.}}
path-canvas.mc-path-canvas.which.note: Accessible name of a curve handle with its position. {which} is the keyword in or out; do not translate the keywords in and other. {n} is the point's position, starting at 1. {x} and {y} are coordinates.

vars.n: The value that replaces n in the text.
vars.which: The value that replaces which in the text.
vars.x: The value that replaces x in the text.
vars.y: The value that replaces y in the text.

path-canvas.mc-path-canvas.which-2.text: {which, select, in {In handle of point {n}.} other {Out handle of point {n}.}}
path-canvas.mc-path-canvas.which-2.note: Same as the other handle name but without coordinates. {which} is the keyword in or out; do not translate the keywords in and other. {n} is the point's position, starting at 1.

vars.n: The value that replaces n in the text.
vars.which: The value that replaces which in the text.

path-canvas.mc-path-canvas.x-x-y-y.note: Position readout. {x} is the horizontal and {y} the vertical coordinate, as numbers.

vars.x: The value that replaces x in the text.
vars.y: The value that replaces y in the text.
